title: SDK integrator checklist & lightweight stub quickstart
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This page is a focused, pragmatic checklist and fast-path quickstart for SDK integrators who need to onboard a new client library into Redwood’s telemetry and runtime ecosystem. The document describes a lightweight stub server pattern that teams can use to validate integration points, test telemetry contracts, and run deterministic smoke tests before pressing a fuller SDK release.

Goals

- Reduce integration friction for third-party SDKs and internal SDK adapters.
- Provide a minimal reproducible runtime (stub) that exercises API, streaming, error, and telemetry paths.
- Make telemetry contracts explicit and testable with automated golden traces.
- Offer a short checklist for production readiness and rollout gating.

When to use this quickstart

- New SDK integration (language or platform) where full runtime is still under active development.
- Porting an existing integration to a new telemetry schema/version.
- Running canary smoke-tests for SDK releases before customer-facing rollout.

Prerequisites

- Access to the Redwood dev cluster or local sandbox.
- Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ (examples provided for both).
- A service account API key with scope: sdk-integration:dev and telemetry:write.
- Docker (optional) for isolating the stub.

Quickstart - high level steps

1) Clone the integrator sandbox
   - git clone git@internal:redwood/sdk-integrator-sandbox.git && cd sdk-integrator-sandbox

2) Start the lightweight stub server (pick language)
   - Node: npm run start:stub-node  # serves /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints
   - Python: poetry run python stub_server.py --port 8080

3) Configure the SDK to point at the stub
   - export RW_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080
   - export RW_API_KEY=<dev-key>

4) Run the SDK smoke harness
   - npm run test:smoke or pytest tests/smoke_test.py

5) Validate telemetry output
   - Run the trace collector: docker run -p 4317:4317 --rm internal/trace-collector:latest
   - Execute smoke tests and confirm golden-trace JSONs are produced under ./goldens/

6) Promote to canary and run runtime load checks
   - Deploy the stub as a canary into the dev namespace and exercise 100 rps for 5 minutes to validate latency and error propagation.

7) Follow production-readiness checklist below before full rollout.

Lightweight stub server - responsibilities

- Accept HTTP 1.1/2 requests on /v1/generate and /v1/stream.
- Support query parameters for model_id, temperature, max_tokens to exercise routing and kernel selection logic.
- Return deterministic token streams when ?seed=NN is provided.
- Emit telemetry spans & metrics that match Redwood contract v2 (see contract example).
- Simulate transient errors: 429 (rate limit), 503 (overload), and JSON Schema validation errors.

Minimal Node stub example (pseudo)

- File: stub-node/index.js
- Key behaviors shown inline for developer reference:

const express = require('express');
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.post('/v1/generate', (req, res) => {
  /* validate headers, emit telemetry span (trace id), return deterministic response */
  const seed = req.query.seed || 'default';
  res.json({request_id: `req-${seed}`, text: `Hello from stub (seed=${seed})`});
});
app.listen(process.env.PORT || 8080);

Shell snippet: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' $RW_API_BASE/v1/generate

Telemetry contract (shape) - Redwood v2 (human-readable)

- Trace span fields (required): trace_id, span_id, parent_id (optional), service.name, operation, start_ns, duration_ns, status.code
- Event attributes (recommended): sdk.version, language, model_id, route, token_count, sampled_rate
- Metric names: sdk.request.count, sdk.request.latency_ms.p95, sdk.tokens.generated.count, sdk.errors.count

Example golden trace (JSON snippet)

{
  "trace_id": "abcd1234ef",
  "spans": [
    {"span_id": "s1", "operation": "client.request", "service.name": "sdk-python", "start_ns": "1680000000000", "duration_ns": "1200000", "attributes": {"model_id": "redwood-mini", "sdk.version": "0.4.1", "token_count": "12"}}
  ]
}

Production-readiness checklist (lightweight)

- Functional tests: all smoke tests pass locally and in CI.
- Telemetry: golden traces match schema; sampling rate defaults to 1% in CI and 100% in dev.
- Error handling: SDK surfaces 429/503 with retryable flags.
- Streaming: stream chunk ordering preserved and finalizing metadata is emitted.
- Security: API key usage verified; logs do not contain full prompts or customer PII.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency under 200ms for generate on dev hardware or documented caveats if not achievable.
- Backwards compatibility: adapter respects previous headers (x-rw-compat) if present.

Testing and validation patterns

- Golden-trace diffing: run ./tools/trace-diff --expected ./goldens/last_release.json --actual ./out/trace.json and fail CI on diffs.
- Fault injection: use the stub query param ?fault=429 to validate SDK retry/backoff logic.
- Load smoke: k6 -u 50 -d 60s --request-body '{"prompt":"stress"}' http://stub:8080/v1/generate

Rollout guidance

- Stage 0: local developer sign-off (author sign-off)
- Stage 1: CI gated tests with golden-trace validation (run on every PR)
- Stage 2: Deploy stub to dev namespace and run canary traffic (5–10% of internal integration traffic)
- Stage 3: Controlled customer canary (opt-in customers) for two weeks with telemetry monitoring
- Stage 4: Full rollout + deprecate stub endpoints in favor of production endpoint mapping

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: Integrations SDK team (rotating owner per language).
- Oncall for canary: eng-sre (page: #canary-alerts).
- Escalation: if telemetry mismatch or missing spans, create a ticket in INTEGRATIONS-OBS and notify observability-oncall.

Common problems & fixes

- Missing spans in traces: ensure SDK initialized tracer with the RW_TRACE_EXPORTER env var; confirm credentials.
- Non-deterministic golden traces: set ?seed=<fixed> in tests and pin sdk.version in test matrix.
- Prompt leakage in logs: enable REDACT_PROMPTS=true and verify through unit tests.

Appendix - supporting commands and configs

- Start trace collector (local): docker run -p 4317:4317 internal/trace-collector:latest
- Local env file example (.env.local):
  RW_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080
  RW_API_KEY=dev-xxxxxxxx
  RW_TRACE_EXPORTER=localhost:4317

- CI job snippets (GitHub Actions step):
  - name: Run smoke tests
    run: |
      npm ci
      npm run test:smoke

References

- SDK telemetry contract v2 (internal doc): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-observability-telemetry-cookbook-2026
- Golden trace tooling: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-regression-goldens-and-diff-runner-playbook-2026

If you are integrating a language/adapter not covered here, open INTEGRATIONS-ONRAMP and assign the integrator template to the new ticket.
